title: Team Development Practices
keywords: legacy php, migration, and professional development
learning_outcomes: Explain what team development practices contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: shared coding standards.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. In this lesson, focus on shared coding standards; then compare it with branching and pull requests. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use team development practices when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Legacy maintenance preserves real behavior while removing risky assumptions. Use tests to make changes incremental, check the supported PHP/dependency matrix, and migrate deprecated patterns with a documented plan. For team development practices, begin with shared coding standards. Also distinguish branching and pull requests; issue tracking; technical discussions. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Change legacy code incrementally, use tests to preserve behavior, and verify the target PHP/dependency compatibility matrix.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for team development practices from top to bottom. Start by identifying shared coding standards, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.

summary: Team Development Practices is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Change legacy code incrementally, use tests to preserve behavior, and verify the target PHP/dependency compatibility matrix.
